# `get_camera_info`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read static camera information for the open camera or a listed camera.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build PURE GETTER, probable) |
| Side-effect tier | B |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xc09c0, GetCamInfo(CAM_INFO*) @0x11df20 (camera mutex, IsOpened else 318), GetCamInfo(int, CAM_INFO*) @0x11e360 (connected-list walk, 318 @0x11e568), img_cam_mipi::GetCamInfo(int) @0x154a60 (cache map lookup, 200 @0x154af4) (64-bit build) |

With no params (or an empty array) returns the currently open camera's info; with an integer ordinal (scalar or first array element) returns the cached discovery metadata of that listed camera without opening it. Fails with 318 when no info is available (camera closed, or ordinal not in the list), and with 200 when the listed camera's id is missing from the info cache. Non-integer params fail with 104. It is a read-only query; it changes no setting, sends no event, persists nothing and moves nothing. Without params it re-reads the open camera's static description from the driver (open, read-direction info ioctl, close) and refreshes the device's cached copy, which is idempotent. Both paths take the camera lock briefly, so the call may wait behind other camera operations (INFERRED from the shared lock). On a live device (2026-10-16) the ordinals 0 and 1 both returned code 0 with all-zero default records (chip [0,0], pixel size 0, all flags false), so both ordinals are listed but their cached metadata was empty at that time (OBSERVED); why it was empty is INFERRED to be a cache that the ordinal path never fills itself. A later no-params call on an idle device returned code 0 with the telescope camera record (chip [2160,3840], pixel 2.9 um, GR, colour, bins [1,2]), and ordinals 0 and 1 stayed all-zero before and after it (OBSERVED 2026-10-16), so the no-params refresh does not fill the ordinal cache. During active imaging (View, Stack and Exposure all working), ordinals 0 and 1 returned the same default records in 11 rounds 60 s apart, while get_device_state in the same session returned filled camera and second_camera snapshots, so imaging does not fill the per-ordinal cache either (OBSERVED 2026-10-18; the session did not record the firmware version, and the device has run 9.75 since 2026-10-16).

Side effects: In the 64-bit build the current-camera lookup queries the driver (device node opened, info ioctl, closed), refreshes the shared camera metadata record and may log; the ordinal branch reads the discovery cache. Both take the camera mutex. No camera setting is changed and no event is sent.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_camera_info"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Optional camera ordinal. Absent or empty array selects the currently open camera. Any non-integer (including null) fails with 104. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | Params (after array first-element selection) present but not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 318 | Current camera closed, or the ordinal is negative or not in the discovery list | `device not connected` |
| 200 | The ordinal is in the connected list but that camera's id is missing from the info cache; dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 207 | Operation failure whose thread-local error code is zero (the default substituted when the callee set none); other callee-set codes are forwarded unchanged | `fail to operate` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Codes raised by the downstream info lookup are forwarded and not enumerated.

## Example

Request, current:

```json
{"id":36,"method":"get_camera_info"}
```

Request, by-ordinal:

```json
{"id":37,"method":"get_camera_info","params":[0]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_camera_info","result":{"chip_size":[1920,1080],"bins":[1,2],"pixel_size_um":2.9,"unity_gain":80,"has_cooler":false,"is_color":true,"is_usb3_host":true,"has_hpc":false,"debayer_pattern":"GRBG"},"code":0,"id":36}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_camera_info","error":"device not connected","code":318,"id":38}
```
